reference_title: Assuring Quality in Geotechnical Reporting Documents

sections.title: Overview and Purpose
sections.summary: GEC-14 provides guidance for State DOTs and transportation agencies to incorporate Quality Assurance (QA) into the preparation of Geotechnical Reporting Documents (GRDs). GRDs include reports and documents that communicate geotechnical data, analyses, and recommendations. The document addresses quality of subsurface investigations, data analysis, design analyses, and constructability considerations. Scope is limited to QA during the Design Development phase — not QA during construction. Addresses all Alternative Contracting Methods (ACMs): Design-Bid-Build (DBB), Design-Build (DB), and Construction Manager/General Contractor (CM/GC).
sections.body:
This document provides assistance to effectively incorporate Quality Assurance (QA) into the preparation of Geotechnical Reporting Documents (GRDs), which includes reports and other documents that communicate geotechnical data, analyses and recommendations. It addresses the quality of subsurface investigations, data summary and analysis, use of appropriate design analyses, incorporation of performance requirements, and consideration of constructability in design and construction documents.

Scope limitation: QA of construction plans (verification of design intent in PS&E) is not within scope. QA during construction is not within scope. However, the importance of continued coordination between design and construction staff is acknowledged.

GRD types include: Geotechnical Data Reports, Geotechnical Baseline Reports, Foundation Reports, Geotechnical Design Memos, and others defined by owner agencies. Multiple GRDs may be required for one project due to owner practices, project phasing, modifications to project scope, and use of ACMs.

Key components and objectives of GEC-14: (1) outline work elements, parties, and relationships in various ADMs and ACMs from project development to construction documents; (2) complete review of owner agency role in preparing bidding documents; (3) incorporate considerations for owner agency QA needs with all ACMs including ATCs; (4) discuss communications between owner and GRD preparers; (5) describe appropriate content, QA, and roles for various ACMs and GRD types; (6) provide guidance for development of QA checklists.
key_points: GEC-14 applies to GRDs during Design Development phase only — not to construction QA
Scope: all ACMs — Design-Bid-Build (DBB), Design-Build (DB), and CM/GC
Multiple GRDs may be required for one project due to phasing, ACM, and scope changes
QA of construction plans (PS&E) is beyond scope — but GS should review plans to verify incorporation
Document builds on FHWA (2003) Checklists and Guidelines publication and FHWA GECs
sections.applicability: QA framework for all types of geotechnical reporting documents in transportation projects

sections.title: Definitions and Key Terminology
sections.summary: Key terms: ACMs = DBB, DB, CM/GC. ADMs = who delivers the GRD (owner staff, design consultant, subconsultant). GRD = broad term for all geotechnical reporting documents. GDR = factual data only, no recommendations (DB bid phase). GBR = contractually binding interpretation; allocates risk between owner and contractor (primarily tunnels). GR = standard design report with recommendations. QC = operational techniques to verify quality requirements. QA = planned activities verifying QC has occurred. GS = Geotechnical Specialist — responsible professional, typically registered in project state.
sections.body:
Key definitions:

Alternative Contracting Methods (ACMs): DBB — traditional; 100% design then bid. DB — design taken to ~30% level; DB Team completes final design and construction after award. CM/GC — owner contracts with design consultant and contractor simultaneously; contractor provides constructability input during design; contract awarded when design is complete if fair price agreed.

Alternative Delivery Methods (ADMs): Who provides the GRDs — owner agency in-house staff, design consultant with in-house GS, design consultant with GS subconsultant, or GS consultant directly.

Geotechnical Data Report (GDR) (ASCE 1997): Factual report included in contract documents. Contains subsurface exploration data, field investigation results, lab test results — without analyses or design recommendations. Used for DB contracts to inform proposal teams.

Geotechnical Baseline Report (GBR) (ASCE 1997): Interpretive report of geotechnical conditions in contract documents. Establishes contractual statement of anticipated conditions. Risks consistent with or less adverse than baseline allocated to contractor; more adverse conditions accepted by owner. Used primarily for tunnel projects.

Geotechnical Report (GR) (FHWA 2003): Tool to communicate site conditions and design/construction recommendations to roadway design, bridge design, and construction personnel.

Geotechnical Reporting Documents (GRDs): Broad term including data reports, engineering reports, foundation investigation reports, baseline reports, design memos, emails. QA must be incorporated into all GRDs.

Geotechnical Specialist (GS): Individual responsible for geotechnical aspects of project design, construction, and monitoring. Typically required to be registered in the project state for DOT projects.

QC: Operational techniques to verify quality requirements — checking, updating, confirming deficiencies resolved. QA: Planned systematic activities verifying QC has been performed.
key_points: DBB: 100% design before bid; DB: ~30% design before bid, DB Team finishes design+construction; CM/GC: contractor joins during design
GDR: factual data only, no recommendations — used in DB bid phase
GBR: contractually binding baseline; risks more adverse than baseline = owner's; primarily used for tunnels
QC = checking for accuracy; QA = verifying that QC was done
GS must be registered in the project state for most DOT projects
sections.applicability: Terminology and definitions for geotechnical reporting quality assurance programs
